An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting an energy-dependent pattern that adheres to a power law with an index of 0.79 ± 0.19. We also discovered that the orientation of these anisotropy patterns supports their extragalactic origins, across all energy levels examined. Furthermore, an investigation of quadrupolar components revealed that they lacked sufficient statistical significance. We interpret our findings within the context of theoretical models proposing the distribution of extremely energetic cosmic sources and cosmic magnetic field dynamics.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident across different centralities and become more pronounced in more central collisions and in collisions where the momentum of the particles is higher than 2 GeV/c. These findings, which have been compared to theoretical models such as iEBE-VISHNU, MUSIC, and AMPT, shed new light on the complex and not well understood initial conditions of these collisions. Furthermore, they highlight unique sensitivities to two crucial factors: the viscosity of quark--gluon plasma and the characteristics of the collisions' initial state. Given that these fluctuations tend to increase with the momentum of the particles, there is a need for re-examining existing theoretical models to gain a more precise and unbiased understanding of quark--gluon plasma's properties.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be associated with a truth status: true, false, inconsistent, or undetermined. Furthermore, our framework facilitates examination of pressing problems like data quality assessments, query validation, and data merging. Specifically, we investigate query validation as the central problem of this research, building on a previous study by presenting methods to: (1) handle inconsistencies beyond binary relationships; (2) apply to data tables that contain missing values; and (3) consider the impact of inconsistencies on data rows. We also propose a novel definition for a critical concept: data repair. Additionally, we provide a characterization for repairability and develop an algorithm for identifying repairable tables. We further define two critical operations: data rejection and data modification - which can be employed to resolve inconsistencies. We provide a method to: i) determine the feasibility of these operations for a given scenario, and where feasible; ii) recommend applicable operations; and where multiple options exist; and iii) select the most suitable approach. To cover a broader scope, this research can be adjusted to: (1) exclude the presence of missing values; and (2) apply to data tables that adhere to specific dependency rules.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrating under mild conditions that maximum likelihood estimation yields reliable and normally-distributed estimates of model parameters. To evaluate the TV-PARX model's performance and forecasting capabilities in real-world scenarios, we conducted a series of Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we have applied the time-varying specification of the TV-PARX model to empirical data sets, analyzing new daily COVID-19 cases in Italy and corporate defaults in the US.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose whose descriptor corresponds to that in the demonstration. NDFs
are efficiently trained without expert input, using a self-supervised 3D
auto-encoder, and exhibit robust performance across 6-DoF rotations and translations.
In experiments, NDFs master tasks from just a handful (5-10) demonstrations,
in both simulation and with a physical robot. Results show our method excels at
generalizing over different object instances and poses, surpassing a comparison
method relying on 2D descriptors. The NDF project is hosted at https://yilundu.github.io/ndf/.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ in the leading order derivative approximation, and and we find the Yang-Lee edge position $z_c$ to be approximately 2.03, 1.62 for $N=2, 4$ in log-derivative approximation.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined quickly, regardless of the system's absolute calibration, and even provides calibration as a by-product. Our team used extensive data from the FRAM telescope at the Pierre Auger Observatory and a similar telescope at the Cherenkov Telescope Array site to improve the precision of this technique to a precision of possibly 0.01. To accomplish this, we conducted precise laboratory measurements of the system's response to varying light intensities and spectra to counter the limitations of non-linear CCD detectors under observation conditions.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters in the initial stage. Object pose is then resolved through the construction of correspondence constraints utilizing these intermediate cues. This study concentrates on refining two-stage pipelines by combining two distinct concepts: projection grouping on one hand and correspondence learning on the other. We initially employ a patch-based method to forecast projection heatmaps, representing the likelihood distribution of projected corners from 3D bounding boxes. Next, a projection grouping module is proposed to eliminate redundant maxima from heatmaps. Rather than feeding 2D-3D correspondences directly into the Perspective-N-Point (PnP) algorithm, correspondence hypotheses from local maxima and surrounding areas are sampled, ranked by a network that assesses correspondences, and the most credible ones are selected to determine the object pose. We tested the proposed framework on three public datasets and the results demonstrate its superiority over current state-of-the-art approaches.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, and Brownian motions. By utilizing the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion, recent studies found that the methods' accuracy could be evaluated in terms of the impact of the step size on the configurational sampling. Comparisons were made between various configurations, finding that for realistic simulations, a specific method recovers the correct distributions for polypeptides, requiring significantly fewer simulations than an efficient alternative. Through a case study on the porphyrin, another molecule, the optimal method required a thousands of times larger step size than the best existing method, achieving nearly the same accuracy. As shown in a viral capsid model, a extremely large system, the best method could recover the correct distributions with a step size over a hundred times larger than the best alternative, again requiring significantly fewer simulations. Ultimately, the assessments demonstrated that the method could recover the correct configurations with a significantly larger allowed step size in viral capsid simulations.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, characterized by a layer of trapped air, is often referred to as the "whoosh" regime but has been observed to begin at higher speeds than previously thought. By measuring the duration of surface seal duration, we found that it applies to a broader range of speeds than what was originally proposed by Mayton and Frash (1966). In contrast to earlier studies, we discovered that the duration of surface seal is influenced by both in-phase and squared driving forces, resulting from surface tension and inertia, respectively. This finding is supported by a new, more accurate dimensionless velocity formula that better aligns with the data collected.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms emerge as crucial elements in these theories. These $\theta$-terms generate nonlinear connections between axion fields and quadratic gauge field strengths which can be used to break many universal symmetries. If we consider charged states as part of the scenario, additional universal symmetries may be destroyed, yet we found that the $\theta$-terms yield a Witten-like effect that indicates that the range of charged states is composed of an endlessly populated, lattice-like spectrum generated through the monodromy transformation, an element of the boundary near which the moduli space is established, and which defines the range of the effective theory.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research and development for both fundamental understanding and applications in metrology and communication. The progress in this area relies heavily on identifying distinct references in energy and phase for experiments involving multiple phonons. High-quality microcavities containing dark excitons are an ideal platform for this endeavor, as the dark excitons, protected from decay by a large energy gap, provide a reference point and are also slow movers, facilitating interactions with multiple phonons. We managed to achieve giant Rabi oscillations with up to eight photons exchanged with the vibrational mode in a AlAs cavity quantum electrodynamics system, demonstrating an eightfold increase in the 8-phonon state splitting compared to the single-phonon state. These results indicate that AlAs cavity quantum electrodynamics systems are a prime setting for exploring the complexities of many-body physics and for developing a coherent multi-phonon standard.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group, specifically focusing on a square lattice with glide symmetries. By applying generic symmetric and antisymmetric constraints to this lattice, we establish the unique pattern for coupling between atoms and determine its application to various materials. These include CrGeTe, NbPAs, and MoPOAs, which initially adopt a 1D structure but adopt unique folded 2D monolayer configurations through the application of in-plane strain. This transformation results in distinct, gapless semi-metallic phases that display four simultaneous Dirac points within the first Brillouin zone.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the properties of SPCCSs, including the effect of catalysis on the quantum fluctuations of the electromagnetic field, as well as their application in quantum metrology and communication. Notably, we reveal the non-classical nature of SPCCSs by analyzing their squeeze and sub-Poissonian characteristics. It is important to highlight that SPCCSs are distinct from other states created through quantum-optical catalysis, as they are uniquely capable of being represented by a single-photon distribution. States denoted as |1><0|ρc to higher-order components are impossible.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of the Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical histories, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and combining these sources of information is time-consuming and sometimes produces inconclusive results. In this study, we investigate the potential for a more streamlined clinical approach that solely utilizes CT scans for automatically identifying and outlining tumors in the esophagus with satisfactory precision. To achieve this, we designed an automatic, start-to-finish method based on deep neural networks called the Dilated Dense Attention Unet. This model leverages spatial and channel attention mechanisms in dense blocks to prioritize specific features and regions. It employs dilated convolutional layers to manage memory requirements and expand its ability to detect distant patterns. We gathered a comprehensive dataset consisting of 792 CT scans from 289 distinct patients with diverse anatomies and included air pockets, feeding tubes, and proximal tumors. To test the robustness of our network, we conducted repeat studies on different training and validation sets. Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal reflectivity. Recent studies have also considered Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles as potential enhancers for hadron therapy treatments of cancer. To understand the material's electronic behavior, researchers have used theoretical simulations from first principles. Yet, Ta$_2$O$_5$'s stable configuration from a crystallographic standpoint remains undetermined. To address this, researchers used statistical methods to identify the most stable Ta$_2$O$_5$ crystal structure state. The results showed that the predicted structure, labeled as Ta$_2$O$_5$_{H}, has higher stability compared to other known forms of tantalum oxide, although it shares similarities with the O$_5$ pyramidal units of the $\delta$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ structure. Furthermore, Ta$_2$O$_5$_{H} exhibits a predicted band gap of 3.00 eV in simulations and 3.05 eV in measurements, and its optical characteristics were also examined in the study.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but ignored a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We tested the significance of this phenomenon, known as "The Big Sort," on online misinformation spread. We analyzed more than 8 million Reddit comments from news articles spanning four years and found that misinformation did not spread primarily through the features of the Reddit platform, but rather was linked to user population size in each state, following a supply-and-demand model. Furthermore, variations in misinformation dissemination were explained by local personality traits and cultural characteristics rather than economic, social, or political conditions. In areas where residents are less diligent in nature, and cultures place little emphasis on adherence to norms, we found increased circulation of all news, including credible sources.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose is essential. This study examines audio input from humans instructing a robot using Sawyer via spoken language by analyzing three key features: speech duration, tone variation, and speech content. Evaluating these features across four dimensions, it was discovered that instructors frequently use the same vocabulary to describe specific task elements despite varying situations such as task types, audio instructions, and errors encountered during demonstrations. However, differences in speech patterns including duration and inflection are present across these conditions, showing that human speech carries significant, potentially valuable information for enhancing robotic learning through demonstration-based methods.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations and their broader integro-differential generalizations, ensuring the well-posedness of state or operator complexity optimization problems. Our comprehensive investigation extends upon our prior findings in arXiv:2005.00664 and journal publications, incorporating a distinct manner of time dependence.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the meaning of utterances.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-target domain recommendation, in which only one target domain contains sparse data, offers a promising solution by leveraging the abundant data from the other domain(s). Despite its potential, current multi-target multi-domain recommendation approaches, which utilize data from multiple target domains, tend to suffer from missing preferences due to the absence of recommendation algorithms designed to handle multi-sparse data across multiple domains. This challenge is exacerbated by the prevalent scarcity of data in both user-side and item-side across the target domains. This paper, which proposes a Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation model named MSDCP, presents an innovative solution to this challenge via a Multi-Domain Comprehensive Preference Learning framework. Specifically, MSDCP employs a sparse-enlightening module to enrich the data in the user-side sparse domain by borrowing relevant information from the item-side sparse domain, and a borrowing-enhancement module to augment the data in the item-side sparse domain by borrowing relevant information from the user-side domain. This paper, which also incorporates two additional borrowing-enhancement modules to handle the data in the non-sparse domains, utilizes a borrowing-enhancement mechanism that borrows complementary data from other domains while preventing negative transfer. Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for a wide range of cones such as projective matrices, paraboloids, and other complex shapes. This work introduces a new conic solver named Hypatia.jl, designed to handle these complex geometric shapes, and showcases its capabilities when working with four distinct cones. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Hypatia.jl by using it to solve various optimization problems, including those involving positive definite matrices, quadratics, and complex geometric shapes.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially for extensive research projects. Several approaches have been explored to develop scalable and dependable QC methods, but effectively applying them to highly diverse and underrepresented population subgroups remains a significant challenge and potential risk. This study evaluated the QC methods' generalizability across diverse population subgroups using nine distinct MRI datasets from different imaging centers and study purposes. It compared the results from training and testing with data from the same and different population subgroups. Our evaluation revealed a significant difference (0.15 on average) between same-subgroup and different sub-group results, indicating poor generalizability of the QC models. It also demonstrated a correlation (0.40) between dataset diversity and model generalizability. These findings highlight the diverse datasets' importance in improving QC models' generalizability across different population subgroups. They call for greater diversity in existing MRI datasets and propose the development of universally applicable QC standards. Otherwise, there's a risk of QC bias in diverse and evolving MRI datasets.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an algebraic reformulation of the problem. Our approach was tested on real-world data from a specific day when a storm caused significant disruptions to the power grid in New York. We examined various scenarios to identify the most effective strategies for coordinating the activation of private electric vehicles and renewable energy sources with grid operators. Furthermore, we analyzed how the behavior of private electric vehicles, specifically their tendency to stay connected to the grid while parked, influences the proposed coordination strategies. Our findings offer valuable insights for enhancing grid resilience and guiding future infrastructure development.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdCmSn3, Cm3Sn3, and Gd3Sn3, as well as the ab initio pseudopotential method used to investigate these properties. According to the results, Gd3Sn3 and Cm3Sn3 adopt the AuCu3 structure type, and both exhibit exchange-narrowed bands and localized 4f (Gd) or 5f (Cm) shells that contribute to their moments. The calculated total energy indicates that Gd3Sn3 and Cm3Sn3 show hexagonal and cubic symmetries, respectively, in addition to examining mixed-valence Gd-Cm compounds like GdCmSn3, Gd2CmSn3, and Gd3CmSn3. The research reveals that GdCmSn3 adopts the AuCu3 structure, and Gd2CmSn3 and Gd3CmSn3 adopt the MgNiSn structure. The 4f and 5f moments interact with the Sn5f/5d and Gd4d/5d states, leading to significant magnetic anisotropy in these compounds.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. For consistency, three fermion families are necessary as indicated by triangle anomaly cancellation and asymptotic freedom. In the bilepton model, novel physical phenomena are predicted to occur, including bileptons and three types of heavy quarks: ${\cal D}$, ${\cal S}$, and ${\cal T}$. Theoretical calculations suggest that Quantum Chromodynamics will result in heavy quarks bonding to each other or light quarks to form composite particles like baryons and mesons that might be detectable with a next-generation 100 TeV particle accelerator but are too heavy for the current LHC.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn. Moreover, we establish a connection between this ordered system and the geometry of the Bn Coxeter system.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio $\Gamma$ and the radial distribution of matter density within haloes $\rho(r)$. Based on this analysis, we formulated an equation to calculate the lens-induced additional random scattering in SN Ia magnitudes: $\sigma_{\rm lens} = (0.06 \pm 0.017) \cdot (d_{\rm C}(z)/ d_{\rm C}(1))^{3/2}$. As a result, the lens-induced apparent magnitude dispersion will approach the same magnitude as intrinsic SN Ia scatter at $z \approx 1.2$. Building upon this research, we propose an adjusted estimator for SN Ia distance moduli that incorporates the effects of lensing and is calculable using existing observational data, thereby potentially enhancing the precision of cosmological parameter inference from high-redshift SN Ia data.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high-quality T center defects in photonic Silicon-On-Insulator material as well. Like their bulk counterparts, these SOI T centers exhibit a distinct optical absorption pattern and long spin lifetimes, as evidenced by experiments. Notably, both types of T center defects have magnetic field insensitivity around the zero field region, facilitating the development of high-speed and long-range quantum communication devices.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into 3 groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the input, another that uses partial
context by isolating part of the feature map, and one that uses full context
without isolation.
Our evaluation method assesses the effect of context for each deep detector
category systematically. A specially designed dataset is created to test the
effect of context for deep detectors. The impact of removing the background
context and foreground objects on the MS COCO is also examined.
It is shown that both two-stage and single-stage object detectors can make use
of the context due to their extensive receptive field.
Thus, selecting the best object detector for a particular application depends
on the specific context in question.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$, within the bounded domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $x$ contains the origin with smooth boundary, and for a certain condition $\beta\in [0,2)$; here $m$ denotes a function that belongs to Kirchhoff type, $f_i$ behave like $e^{\beta s^2}$, and there is a function $h_i\in \left(\big(H^1_0(\Omega)\big)^*,\|\cdot\|_*\right)$. By making use of a singular Trudinger-Moser inequality for a small positive value $\varepsilon$ and variational methods, we are able to establish sufficient conditions for a multiplicity of the system's solutions given the given conditions.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property (SCP) or the strong Rayleigh property (SRP). Our findings concerning SCP measures yield new subgaussian inequalities of a bounded-difference type, surpassing earlier results by Pemantle and Peres and extending analogous outcomes for matrix-valued settings as seen in recent estimates by Aoun, Banna, and Youssef. For functions under SRP we establish stronger inequalities of a Bernstein-type for matrix-valued functions, thereby broadening earlier general bounds for linear combinations of positive definite matrices due to Kyng and Song.

Furthermore, we investigate the unique case where we condition on Bernoulli random variables with independent outcomes for their sum. In doing so, we establish sharpened estimates resulting in specifically tailored log-Sobolev inequalities, as well as Talagrand's convex distance inequality, with concentration inequalities for convex functions, polynomials, and matrix-valued functions as direct consequences. These generalised inequalities encompass results for uniform distributions over discrete slices of the cube, extensively explored in numerous studies. The current approach builds upon recent outcomes from Hermon and Salez as well as on a broader framework involving modified log-Sobolev inequalities within the context of the discrete cube, with independent developments also noted by Banna and Youssef.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties. Patients receiving incompatible transplants face a higher risk of transplant rejection, infections, and cancer, and are more likely to lose their transplants. We aim to find the optimal acceptance criteria for end-stage kidney patients by potentially receiving incompatible kidneys. A Markov Decision Process model is introduced, which accounts for the level of incompatibility as a key factor, making it a more complex problem to solve, but with suitable conditions, it is possible to establish control limit policies that can be easily applied. Our study uses numerical examples to demonstrate how the optimal policy behaves under different levels of incompatibility, and highlights the significance of taking incompatibility into consideration in decision-making, especially when desensitization treatments are available.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical examination of the word2vec model, particularly in its implementation with the Skip-gram learning method. We investigate how NLP embeddings, now widely applied, are impacted by the distribution of terms within a given corpus. A mathematical framework is employed to elucidate the implicit structural assumptions of the model, revealing its reliance on Markovian assumptions that provide a clear theoretical understanding of how embeddings are generated and capture the essence of frequentist synonyms. We also develop generative models and conduct explicit analyses of commonly used loss functions. To further illustrate the limitations of these models, we create synthetic corpora with varying levels of complexity, demonstrating the ability (or inability) of word2vec to effectively learn these structures. We also empirically assess the capabilities of these models using a subset of 10,000 LinkedIn texts from the Loughran-McDonald Financial NLP Sentiment Dataset. Our study includes a proposed robustness test, along with statistical results and visualizations, to better understand the models' performance in capturing intricate patterns in data.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding equilibria, learning rationalizable behavior is another significant goal. However, in contrast to rationality, Nash equilibrium strategies require agents to anticipate and account for the strategies of other players in the game. We introduce a novel multiagent learning algorithm that guarantees convergence to a rationalizable NE. Specifically, our method ensures that the population's strategy distribution will converge to a NE strategy profile where each player is playing a best response to the observed population distribution. We demonstrate the robustness of our approach on both cooperative and competitive multiplayer games, showing that it leads to near-optimal outcomes in cooperative games and high utility outcomes in zero-sum games. We also establish a relationship between our method and the Joint Equilibrium Unlearning (JEU) algorithm, which was previously developed for single-player games.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs of key properties of the model, particularly its early stages and the phase where the epidemic spreads rapidly. They also found that under certain conditions, there are sharp thresholds where the model suddenly switches between two completely different behaviours. It has been proven that these transitions are more dramatic if the model is changed to only form new connections to uninfected individuals, where the model suddenly switches from no infections to complete spread.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurately fitting probability density functions. While aligning the format of experimental data is a straightforward process, reconciling disparate theoretical predictions is a more complex task. Given the numerous PDF fitting projects underway, it is essential to develop a unified approach to Reaching this integration goal. We propose a modular pipeline consisting of five key components: data acquisition, pre-processing, simulation of measurements, extraction of observables and their correlations, and the fitting procedure itself. Each module is designed to be independent, allowing them to be developed separately and integrated seamlessly. This approach is illustrated using two key projects, AQI and OPAL, which serve as building blocks in the pipeline.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations. However, as the number of factors influencing the target outcome grows, the significance of previously collected observations declines rapidly due to their increasing variance. We discover that the standard experience replay method overestimates the potential value of past data and propose a new approach, Variance Reduction based Experience Replay (VEX), which leverages the target variance to evaluate the usefulness of historical observations. Numerical simulations and a real-world supply chain optimization study show that the VEX method accurately selects past observations and provides a faster, more effective alternative to the standard method. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical application of VEX in the supply chain optimization context.

In our analysis of conversational dialogue, we face numerous possible responses 
to any given history, leading us to present the MultiTalk Dataset. This large 
dataset comprises over 320,000 written conversational dialogue sentences, 
maintaining a high degree of complexity (a 12-way branching factor) along with 
6 conversation turns through strategically chosen continuation branches. Our study 
of dialogue generation involves multiple advancements, particularly in highly 
branching scenarios. To evaluate the diversity of generated text, we introduce a 
simple yet effective measurement method grounded in text embedding spaces. 
Otherwise known as the cosine similarity score, this approach assesses the 
variety of conversational responses. Our research also explores various stimulus 
types that influence conversation diversity, as well as the computational 
capabilities required for text generation. In turn, we present a large model 
known as Multitalk-1 through K-step prompting, demonstrating an efficient 
approach in generating diverse text over multiple sentence outputs.

We introduce MG-GLAM, a computational tool developed to rapidly create comprehensive N-body simulations for various cosmological theories, specifically modified gravity models. This program builds upon the existing GLAM code and incorporates an advanced multigrid method to solve the non-linear equations characteristic of modified gravity theories, resulting in highly efficient simulations. For $f(R)$ gravity, MG-GLAM includes multiple variations that mimic distinct behaviors of these models and offers tailored algorithms that significantly reduce computational time and memory usage. This code and its modified GLAM simulations provide a reliable and consistent framework for investigating the effects of modified gravity on the formation of cosmic structures. We demonstrate the code's capability to solve a broad range of modified gravity models by comparing N-body simulations of $f(R)$ gravity to existing ghost-field simulations and analytical predictions of modified power spectra and growth factors. Furthermore, MG-GLAM is an adaptable code that can be easily extended to incorporate other multigrid-based modified gravity models, making it a valuable resource for researchers in this field.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pair consisting of Gaussian free fields and multiple chordal Schramm-Loewev evolution processes in their 2018 study. Building on this research, we develop an analogous definition for rotation-invariant imaginary surfaces as the pair of Gaussian free fields and mutually avoiding stochastic processes in section 3 of this paper. Using the Coulomb gas conformal field theory, we establish the consistency of our definition with that of Miller and Sheffield, thereby proving the existence of a rotation-invariant imaginary surface. We then demonstrate the connection between the system of mutually avoiding processes and the system of lozenges-driven processes as shown in O'Connell's 2012 study. Finally, we show that the system of lozenges-driven processes is local and has no drift, thereby providing a localized model of interacting sub-Riemannian gases with repulsion.

MediaWiki's 'WorkingWiki' is an open-source extension that converts a wiki
into a sophisticated collaborative platform for developing high-quality manuscripts
and software projects. Originally developed at McMaster University's theoretical
biology lab, WorkingWiki enables multiple users to work together on a range of
tasks by utilizing command-line tools to translate raw'source code' into desired outputs.
Its features cater specifically to programmers and researchers who use languages
like R, Python, and C, and it boasts specialized tools for seamless LaTeX editing.
By integrating features from collaborative editors, development environments,
version control systems, and publishing platforms, WorkingWiki unlocks the
full potential of wiki-based collaboration, and its customizable'makefiles'
and modular architecture enable users to tailor and repurpose its functionality.

This study undertakes a linear analysis of a methane-air jet flame experiencing turbulence to determine its response to acoustic vibrations emitted from upstream, while factoring in temperature fluctuations that may breach the assumptions of linear theory near the flame's mouth. An recently developed active flame method is utilized to simulate these variations using an approach that is nearly as accurate as the direct computational fluid dynamics method but with significantly reduced computational costs. This method incorporates a new, robust model for cracking the seal of jet flame turbulence in the early stages. The simulated results are then compared to those from detailed direct simulations, showing that the active flame approach accurately predicts temperature fluctuations, flow patterns, and thermal instability frequencies, while also requiring a relatively low computational costs. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that despite local non-linearity effects, the linear analysis framework is highly effective in predicting the flame's behavior, including its dynamic responses, dynamic instability frequencies, and dynamic vortex shedding. This approach also shows that directing the jet flame turbulence causes it to curl and fold, thus causing it to burn itself and causing significant losses. We investigate the neutrinoless double beta decay driven by an extremely light dark matter field interacting with neutrinos, particularly focusing on the impact when this interaction breaches the lepton number, which directly leads to a significant influence on the $0
u  eta  eta$ decay, even when neutrino masses are very small. Since the ultralight dark matter can be adequately modeled as a classical field, this interaction's effect is reflected in a periodic modification of the $0 
u  eta  eta$ decay rate. We derive the general formula for the decay rate and its expected oscillation amplitude. Furthermore, we incorporate the impact of cosmological constraints on the dark matter parameter space, considering the additional dark matter produced through neutrino decay in the early universe. We find that the relevant combination of the dark matter parameters must have an extremely small value. As a result, the interaction's effect on the decay rate is projected to be minimal but potentially observable as a slight increase in events, offering a very limited possibility for future experiments to detect the dark matter directly. We also consider the influence of this interaction on the $0 
u  eta  eta$ mass scale predicted by natural neutrino models.

Nonlocal gravity theory is a classical generalization of Einstein's gravity theory. Based on an analogy with nonlocal electrodynamics, this new model involves a history-dependent relation that can be confirmed through data. The purpose of this paper is to modify nonlocal gravity theory so that the nonlocal aspect relates directly to observable properties, similar to the approach in nonlocal electrodynamics. The reformulated theory results in a constitutive relation identical to one proposed recently by Puetzfeld, Obukhov, and Hehl. The nonlocal gravity theory can be applied to show that de Sitter spacetime does not meet the theory's requirements.

Understanding how genomic elements affect specific traits through genome-wide association studies remains complex due to the sheer number of available annotations. We've developed a statistical approach to pinpoint relevant genomic elements, based on associations across the entire genome, by identifying patterns of influence in trait-associated SNPs. This approach can incorporate multiple annotation types and has been successfully applied to eighteen human traits such as blood, platelet counts, metabolism-related disorders, height, obesity and a bowel disease, by examining 450 distinct genomic features across one hundred plus tissues and cells types. Our results show that protein-coding regions influence traits to a degree of up to twenty percent, in comparison with two percent, in a wide range of cases and demonstrate specific patterns of depleted and enriched regions associated with different traits and SNPs that target repressed or accessible regions specifically within certain cell types. Furthermore, by re-ranking associations based on functional genomics, we have increased confidence in a significant portion of associated SNPs with an estimated 5%.

This paper discusses recent findings from the LHC involving small systems studied
by the ALICE, ATLAS and CMS collaborations. Due to the growing significance
of QCD in small systems, particularly in situations with high multiplicity, not
all pertinent research can be covered within this report. It primarily examines
measurements focusing on collective behavior in small systems and new results on
strangeness enhancement observed in proton-proton interactions. It is essential to
note that many notable findings have been excluded from the discussion presented
here.

Observations of some variable X-ray sources within the Milky Way's center that have shown no outbursts in over a decade have led some researchers to suggest a significant population of stellar mass black holes in the region. A crucial aspect of the theory that these sources are actually black holes is the claim that neutron star binaries with low masses exhibit recurring X-ray bursts within short intervals. This study contradicts that idea by revealing that about half of the known LMXBs, featuring a neutron star as the primary component, exhibit outburst recurrence times exceeding a decade when detected by the MAXI telescope. Moreover, to reconcile the total population of neutron star binaries with observed and radio pulsar populations within the Milky Way, researchers find that a significant majority of these binaries have recurrence times exceeding a century for outbursts visible to the MAXI telescope and most remain undiscovered.

THz radiation enables the precise stimulation of vibrational frequencies in molecules and crystals, leading to the introduction of inertial influences on electrons. By drawing a comparison to classical mechanics, where circular motion generates Coriolis and centrifugal forces, analogous effects arise, specifically spin-rotation coupling, centrifugal field coupling, and the interplay of these forces with the spin-orbit and the redshift of energy levels. These effects can persist for a few picoseconds following the initial stimulation, and potentially amplifying their magnitude could make this approach a promising means of controlling localized quantum states and chemical reaction barriers via vibration.

Improving neural conversational agents' ability to produce diverse, engaging responses in casual conversations is a challenge. To tackle this issue, this paper introduces two significant innovations. Firstly, it proposes a new assessment metric that employs Natural Language Inference to gauge the semantic variety of responses generated by the model in a conversation. Using a previously established model for this purpose, this metric integrates semantic diversity into an optimization framework, incorporating it as a minimization criterion in conversations. Moreover, this approach is adaptable, allowing for n-way diversity calculations. Our experiments demonstrate that this method compares favorably to existing solutions in terms of response quality and semantic variety. Secondly, this work integrates both word-level and sentence-level diversity measures to create a comprehensive evaluation of model performance. This combined approach ensures a more balanced assessment of the model's generated responses, taking into consideration both the variety of individual words and the overall content of the responses.

The occurrence of sustainable hydrogen burning in very low-mass stars might be impacted by rotation due to the addition of centrifugal force and potential break-up caused by rapid spinning. Computer simulations model rotating low-mass stars with the capability for sustained nuclear reactions, considering a range of rotation rates, and also object with no fuel remaining. Results from simulations were found to match established findings when rotation was absent, but demonstrated that sustained nuclear burning could persist even with rapid spinning, although there were objects that shed mass as a result. The simulations demonstrated that sustained nuclear burning in rotating objects occurs between the marginal break-up point and the point where orbiting fragments could sustain nuclear burning, and also found that the minimum mass for sustained nuclear burning could be increased with spinning, by as much as 17% for slow rotation and up to 96% for extreme rotation. There was an observed drop in the envelope temperature as the speed of rotation increased, which could be attributed to cooling from the enhanced size and expansion of the object, or reduced centrifugal force as the objects moved further from the center of mass.

The technique of amplitude analysis in hadron decay studies is quite effective, 
However, this analysis faces a major challenge in addressing instrumental influences 
such as fluctuations in background levels and selection efficiency across different 
multidimensional kinematic scenarios.  This article will review traditional methods 
used for calculating efficiency and background probability and discuss the application 
of two techniques specifically density estimation using Gaussian processes and 
artificial neural networks. Although widely adopted in other contexts, these methods 
have not been heavily employed for amplitude analyses. The article also introduces 
new applications for these models, such as leveraging sidebands to determine the 
density of background in multiple dimensions, as well as more comprehensive density 
estimation utilizing artificial neural networks.

A new model based on a comprehensive expression for radiation energy has been proposed, and it effectively elucidates the dynamics of afterglows in multiple contexts, including relativistic, non-relativistic phases and fireball radiations with radiative and adiabatic components.

Bipartite graphs depicting connections between distinct groups of objects have numerous practical applications, and their visualization often takes the form of a 2-tier layout where corresponding entities are aligned horizontally across two parallel lines, connected by lines representing relationships between them. The task of reducing edge crossings within these visualizations can be computationally intensive, yet might not always guarantee sufficiently low crossings levels to maintain the visualization's clarity. In contrast, an approach has been developed to remove edge crossings by splitting specific nodes, targeting the minimum number required to yield an edge-free (planar) drawing. The question of determining if an edge-free representation exists after breaking at most a specified number of nodes is related to a more complex variant of the node separation problem, but can be done in a time frame that grows factorially with this number in relation to the input size. This paper presents an improved algorithm with a more manageable exponential growth, and also tackles a more restrictive scenario where the removed lines must belong to particular nodes.

This paper will present our approach to optimizing bipedal robot walking assisted by thrusters using a closed-loop feedback system. By assuming that supervisory controllers are available, which define standard thruster-assisted
locomotion frameworks, our primary concern is efficiently and accurately minimizing performance losses caused by variable jet forces through real-time adjustments of joint positions and velocities. To accomplish this, we will present two key elements: first, the utilization of Model Predictive Control (MPC) to address the complexities of non-linear joint dynamics; and second, the integration of real-time safety assessments to ensure compliance with both the robot's physical limitations and the specific constraints of each thruster. To demonstrate the practical applications of this method, we will also include locomotion results obtained from an actual fully actuated bipedal robot equipped with two thrusters mounted on its lower legs.

Becker-Denef-Lipschitz first observed in 1979 that over finite fields $k$, the total residue map $\text{res}$ from Laurent series to $k$ is expressible in a specific language, provided $t$ is included as a parameter. This discovery motivated further research into the properties of a specific mathematical theory related to valued fields. In the course of these investigations, the authors proved that this theory does not have a certain desirable feature and demonstrated that, for infinite fields $k$, the associated power series fields cannot be computationally decided. This, in turn, led to an analogous undecidability conclusion for a specific type of valued field.

In order to enhance side-channel attacks, this research introduces a new technique, HyperDegrade, which incorporates previous methods and employs simultaneous multithreading architectures.  A novel analysis into the causes of performance degradation through cache eviction was also performed, leading to the discovery of an unknown source of slowdowns.  Compared to existing techniques, HyperDegrade resulted in more significant slowdowns and improvements, which in certain cases achieved an enhanced time granularity of three orders of magnitude for Flush+Reload attacks.  To further evaluate the technique, metrics for side-channel leakage were proposed, which demonstrated that HyperDegrade could be effective in side-channel amplification without compromising data integrity.  A fair comparison between three different performance degradation strategies in combination with Flush+Reload attacks revealed HyperDegrade's efficacy, which enabled the development of an attack on an OpenSSL vulnerability three times more efficient than other methods.  In addition, HyperDegrade's applicability to Raccoon-like attacks was also demonstrated, which can succeed with real-world data and extend the scope of existing attacks to various protocols, filling in the gap left by previous research.

A localized alteration in knot diagrams is referred to as an unknotting operation. It can be demonstrated that any knot diagram can be converted into a trivial unknot through a sequence of unknotting operations, combined with some variations in the diagram configuration, which are referred to as Reidemeister moves. Unknotting operations hold significant value in the field of knot theory; they serve a purpose in the analysis of the structural properties of knots and also have applications in the study of biological molecules, particularly those belonging to the class of polymers and DNA. One such commonly studied operation is the crossing change, first introduced by Cayley in 1859. The aim of this research is to present a novel class of unknotting operations for classical and welded knots, which are referred to as the n-glide changes, first presented in this paper. It was discovered that the glide change belongs to the category of unknotting operations applicable to both classical and virtual links, in contrast to the crossing change, which is limited to the classical case only. Additionally, research questions were presented and various invariants were examined under the influence of the n-glide change.

This is a significant finding. Moreover, this result is independent of, but conceptually and formally distinct from, Conca and Vanasse's result, which arrived at the same conclusion through an independent approach. In cooperative systems with multiple agents, coordination enables tasks to be performed that would be beyond the capabilities of any single agent. We investigate the concept of coordination through strategic decision-making, focusing on a scenario where agents select between two tasks of varying difficulty that are randomly distributed and partially known. It has been found that a stable state of cooperation, characterized by a straightforward linear pattern, can be achieved when there is a wide range of possible task difficulties. Furthermore, it was discovered that the most advantageous action for each agent in response to an approachable strategy profile can be complex and nonlinear when the distribution of task difficulties is not uniform. A computational method has been established to calculate a cooperative equilibrium through learning within the set of linear policy options.

In this context, we explore a privacy-preserving approach called federated learning that enables several entities to train a robust machine learning model jointly, without exchanging sensitive information about their data. Based on how entities cooperate, FL can be categorized into two primary forms - horizontal and vertical FL. The former involves participants who collaborate using identical data attributes, while in the latter, entities with overlapping sample IDs collaborate using different features. Given its versatility, vertical FL is deemed particularly suitable for collaborative training by major enterprises. Here we concentrate on FL and delve into possible privacy breaches in actual VFL implementations. Two applicable attacks were created by us - one is called a reverse multiplication attack designed to circumvent logistic regression, while the other, known as a reverse sum attack, targets XGBoost data preprocessing. Our experiments validate that both attacks are successful, efficient, and can be easily adapted to other settings of VFL.

Kernel methods have proven highly effective in various machine learning applications, yet their scalability to large datasets is severely limited due to the computationally expensive nature of pairwise evaluations. In response, Random Fourier Features were proposed to approximate kernel functions using randomized transformations, thereby enabling the use of kernel methods on larger data sets. While widely adopted, this method has significant drawbacks, notably requiring an unnecessarily large number of features, directly proportional to the size of the dataset, in order to achieve satisfactory results comparable to traditional kernel-based methods. In order to circumvent these limitations and efficiently process large datasets, this paper introduces an alternative method of kernel approximation that leverages insights specific to the underlying data and offers both feature dimensionality reduction and performance enhancements. We test and evaluate this novel method against a range of competitors, including RFF, orthogonal random features, and the Nyström method.

In our study, we demonstrated how both a group that operates on a set in a recurring manner and a diagonal group are effectively incorporated into the wreath products under their combined, or product action, utilizing the Cartesian Decomposition technique.

This research paper examines conformally flat hypersurfaces of n-dimensional space (n is 4 or higher) within a hypersphere of n+2 dimensions. We start by classifying and describing these conformally flat hypersurfaces when they have constant M\"obius curvature under specific transformations. Next, we prove that a compact hypersurface with this constant M\"obius curvature, denoted R, has a specific value determined by the dimension (4R if n equals 4, otherwise R).

A new method of efficient wireless communication is proposed in a novel SWIPT system, enabling faster and more sustainable mobile data networks. The system, utilizing energy-harvesting technology from access points without the need for a splitter, allocates part of the frequency spectrum for information transmission and the remaining for energy capture. To analyze performance improvements, an optimization problem was created that maximizes energy gain and maintains a minimum data rate in a multi-user OFDMA network. Next, the model was refined to investigate throughput optimization in an SWIPT-enabled OFDMA system, resulting in a complex MINLP problem. Finally, an innovative harvesting technique based on a co-located receiver architecture and Generalized Antenna-Switching Technique was explored to improve the energy gain of existing networks.

Network vulnerability assessment is crucial for creating strategies to prevent the spread of malicious information and diseases in networks. Researchers often study network immunization, but traditional approaches typically focus on broad measures, such as network criticality and component size. In contrast, this paper delves into a micro-level analysis, where the removal of individual nodes during an attack is examined in detail. Based on percolation theory, the authors analyze the effects of removing a single node that has the potential to disconnect large portions of the network. Specifically, they investigate the size of these disconnection components for a Cayley tree network. However, existing research has limited data on this topic, and as a result, the authors discover that the number of nodes that can be disconnected follows an exponential distribution characterized by two parameters. These parameters are derived analytically and are found to be directly related to the number of inactive links and the branching factor of the network.

The detection capabilities of advanced gravitational wave detectors are hindered in the high-frequency range by the quantum limitations of measurement and signal loss in optical recycling systems. Overcoming this constraint is critical for identifying gravitational waves generated by binary neutron star mergers. We present the concept of the sloshing Sagnac interferometer topology, an innovative variation of the Michelson design where the end mirrors are optically linked to form an additional resonating cavity. By transforming the detector into a system with multiple coupled cavities, this design outperforms the conventional signal-recycled Michelson setup by overcoming optical loss-induced limitations. Using advanced parameters similar to LIGO+, this new design offers improved sensitivity at high frequencies or better signal-to-noise ratios for specific binary neutron star merger waveforms, offering promising possibilities for future gravitational wave detectors.

Recent large-scale MIMO systems are considered an exciting development, capable of providing rapid data transfer in crowded environments. As a result of their substantial size, MIMO arrays are subject to space-based disruptions and varying ranges that affect how data is perceived by nearby devices. With a high number of devices often present in applications for these systems and the scarcity of pilot signals available for them, designing protocols and scheduling algorithms is increasingly complex. To address this challenge, a new joint protocol has been developed that leverages varying reception areas of devices for better access and prioritizes the scheduling of devices with distinct reception areas for more efficient signal sharing. According to the results obtained, this new scheme delivers considerable gains over traditional approaches in terms of overall connectivity, reduces data transfer delays, and significantly boosts overall connectivity.

Recent observations at sub-millimeter/millimeter wavelengths have revealed that the morphological structure of young stars' surrounding disks comprise various shapes, including symmetrical patterns and features resembling spiral arms, and localized curved formations. Prior research primarily focused on modeling planetary interactions to explain observed patterns in disks. Although some exoplanets have been identified in such systems, many of these substructures emerge even before planetary formation as necessary precursors that lead to the creation of small solid particles, and ultimately, planetesimals. This work employs high-resolution, three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamic simulations that model the gas and solid particle interactions in protoplanetary disks. It highlights the distribution of small solid particles, formed through the vertical shear instability, and suggests that their characteristics align with features observed in recent sub-mm/mm wavelength observations. It also predicts findings that future observations with higher sensitivity and resolution will uncover with the aid of advanced telescopes like ALMA and a Next Generation Very Large Array.

A question remains regarding the secondary component of GW190814 - whether it's a neutron star or a black hole of minimal mass. Researchers have introduced an energy functional based on the density of quark and baryon phases to explore this mystery, leveraging the successful application of PB21opf and BW21 parametrisations in describing GW190814. By employing the Bayesian method and drawing on Bayesian priors and relativistic energy density constraints, key parameters of the quark phase were determined. Subsequently, the resonance energy, effective mass to bare mass ratio, and effective baryon number of baryon phase were set. The resulting parametrisation was then utilised to examine the equation of state, radius, and tidal deformability of relevant neutron stars in the binary system, as well as solitary neutron stars. Furthermore, the parameters of this quark phase model were integrated into RPS-20 and BW20 skyrmes to form a six-body phase diagram.
