A novel adaptive random walk learning algorithm is introduced and proven to converge theoretically. Moreover, our results demonstrate its superior performance compared to other random walk algorithms.

Individuals within the criminal justice system frequently suffer from mental health disorders.  An analysis of North Carolina court cases between 1994 and 2009 examined how court-ordered mental health treatment as part of probation affects an offender's chances of returning to the justice system.  The study focused on returned offenders within a one-year period after their initial release.  It discovered that for every $1 of spending on mental health treatment, there is $2.13 saved by preventing recidivism.  The cost-effectiveness varies by gender, with women showing greater savings of $4.68 in revenue for each $1 spent, compared to men at $1.95 saved.  The analysis also differentiated between violent and non-violent crimes, with violent crimes exhibiting a lower return on investment.  Of the methods used to measure outcomes, the findings from revenue matching produced the most reliable results with a one-year window, whereas other methods used in similar studies resulted from health issues with a one-year window. used to measure outcomes, find findings from revenue matching produce most reliable outcomes with a one-year window, similar studies result from health issues with a one-year window.

A pervasive issue in medical image segmentation tasks is the lack of detailed pixel-level annotation. This paper introduces a new regularization technique, combining interpolation methods to enhance semi-supervised medical image segmentation. The proposed strategy uses consistency regularization to ensure the segmentation of mixed data matches the mixed segmentations. This approach belongs to the category of adaptive data regularization techniques that reduce overfitting when working with highly confident labelled data. The method has several advantages over alternative techniques such as adversarial and generative models, primarily due to its minimal computational requirements. Evaluations using publicly available MRI datasets - specifically ACDC and MMWHS - demonstrate that this proposed technique outperforms existing semi-supervised models, with source code available on GitHub.

To gain a deeper understanding of the performance and lifespan of materials, 
it's crucial to assess their atomic disorder. To this end, we have developed an 
alternative method that leverages a graph neural network to predict the electrical 
resistivity of pure and alloyed metals and semiconductors with multiple element 
compositions. By examining the internal structure of the network, we have been able 
to extract a disorder metric that works well for the pure materials as well. 
Surprisingly, this metric's values match the established Hume-Rothery radius 
standard deviation. Moreover, when used in a single-variable fit, it accurately 
predicts the resistivity of the pure elements. In addition to this, our model and 
our disorder metric have been tested with a comprehensive dataset comprising over 
30,000 materials in the WebElements period table.

Consider a parametric family of distributions defined by $f(y|\theta)$ where $\theta$ is a parameter from the set $\Omega$, a function $\eta(\theta)$ and an unknown distribution $G$ as the mixing distribution. It is necessary to estimate the expected value of $\eta(\theta)$ based on a mixing distribution, denoted as $\eta_G$, using independent observations of $Y_1,...,Y_n$ where each observation follows $f(y|\theta_i)$ and the associated parameters $\theta_i$ follow the distribution $G$ independently. This work delves into finding MLE $\eta_G^*$ to estimate the expected value of $\eta(\theta)$. It is shown that under certain conditions, the MLE consistently estimates the true expected value of $\eta(\theta)$. We also develop a method for constructing the estimation interval of $ \eta_G^ $ and provide some useful applications of this approach to sampling.

Knowledge tracing has seen significant advancements through deep learning-based models, however the underlying factors behind their success remain poorly understood. A primary challenge lies in comparing these approaches, due to the lack of standardization in data preprocessing procedures and evaluation protocols. These inconsistencies hinder real-world applicability in educational settings. To address these limitations, we present PyKT, a comprehensive Python-based platform for valid and standardized evaluations of deep learning-based knowledge tracing methods. This platform incorporates a unified data preprocessing protocol, carefully tested implementations of prominent deep learning models, including DKT, FMT, and FISH, and features customizations for various evaluation protocols. We provide real-world examples of utilizing the pyKT platform for specific deep learning-based KT approaches. This paper also explores the critical issue of model interpretability in deep learning-based knowledge tracing.

Given any manifold $M$, we demonstrate that a second-order elliptic differential operator $P$ possesses closed range in $C^\infty(M)$. Additionally, if the manifold $M$ does not consist of any compact components, it follows that $P$ is surjective within $C^\infty(M)$. This is accompanied by an exploration of its applications to Helmholtz decomposition.

Ten years ago, at the inaugural PxTP workshop, veriT's proof format debuted,  
which has undergone significant evolution ever since. veriT's proofs have found a  
wide range of applications and numerous solvers now generate proofs in this same  
format. As the next step in further improvement, we would like to hear feedback  
from the community to guide upcoming developments in this area. This feedback will  
be utilized in looking at the format's past progression, presenting the approach  
that guided its development, as well as the problems other solvers may experience  
in utilizing it.

As the number of devices contributing to cross-device federated learning grows, synchronizing updates can significantly reduce efficiency. The FedBuff algorithm mitigates this limitation by enabling asynchronous updates and securely aggregated data sharing, thus improving scalability while protecting user privacy. Building on the FedBuff framework for asynchronous learning, this study enhances existing research by relaxing the requirement that the gradient magnitude must remain within predefined bounds. Theoretical convergence rate analysis of the modified FedBuff algorithm considers factors like diverse data sets, varying batch sizes, and delay intervals.

Recently, end-to-end neural automatic speech recognition systems have achieved high accuracy, however, these systems demand considerable amounts of data and advanced computational power. Transfer learning has been proposed to overcome such challenges even across linguistic barriers, for example using a trained English model for German ASR. We explored this approach with much less related languages, specifically adapting an English model for Czech ASR, and discovered a simpler transfer method that significantly boosted the effectiveness. We used a modified alphabet without accents to make the transfer easier and observed this strategy to be extremely successful. Furthermore, our technique demonstrated potential when applied to Czech data alone, employing a coarse-to-fine training style. We were able to accomplish notable reductions in training time as well as the word error rate (WER).

Our novel TD learning approach overcomes several challenges robots encounter when navigating underwater.  By leveraging Gaussian Process regression, our method significantly boosts data efficiency by limiting TD updates.  To facilitate online predictions, we developed a new sparse approximation technique with enhanced performance compared to current rejection-based methods.  By deriving the posterior of the value function and utilizing its moments, we developed SPGP-SARSA: a new algorithm for offline policy evaluation.  Our results show that SPGP-SARSA outperforms the existing state-of-the-art in sparse methods and matches the accuracy of its precise equivalent while successfully being applied to underwater navigation.  Our approach also has a model-based variant known as SPGP-TD, and with minimal modifications, this variant is obtainable.  Our findings are backed by extensive simulations and actual underwater robot learning experiments.

We employ a 1+1+2 covariant semi-tetrad method to describe a static and spherically symmetric relativistic star comprising two fluids with anisotropic pressures, leading to the derivation of anisotropic Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations in covariant form. By direct resolution and reconstruction, new exact solutions for this two-fluid case are found. Additionally, three theorems applicable to the single-fluid scenario can be adapted to yield two-fluid solutions from their single-fluid counterparts.

Most current sequence-to-sequence based Grammatical Error Correction methods focus primarily on generating more pseudo data to improve performance. In contrast, little work has been done adapting GEC models to new domains with limited resources. This study proposes a novel approach using meta-learning to adapt GEC models to unseen domains with few examples. We hypothesize that a domain adapted GEC model via meta-learning achieves better generalization capability on undseen domains. To validate this hypothesis, we conduct experiments on several cross-domain datasets and demonstrate that a domain adapted GEC model via meta-learning outperforms a traditional pseudo data based domain adaptation method even when only a small amount of domain-adapted training data is available. Furthermore, our results show a significant improvement in performance as more domain adapted training data is obtained, demonstrating the strong potential of meta-learning for few-shot domain adaptation in GEC.

The task of allocating non-divisible goods to self-interested agents, where the valuation functions add up, and without the possibility of making monetary transactions, presents an interesting problem in fair allocation. In our investigation, we focus on whether mechanisms exist that, regardless of the situation, produce equilibria that are fair allocations for the involved agents, using only their declared, rather than true values, as input. Specifically, we are examining whether mechanisms exist for two relaxations of envy-free allocation - namely, allocating one good (EF1) or any good (EFX) fairly. Through our exploration, we investigated two established methods for achieving these relaxed envy-free allocations in a non-selfish setting: Round-Robin, known for generating allocations that are fair up to one good for any number of agents, and a cut-and-choose method of Plaut and Roughgarden, known for generating allocations that are fair up to any good for two agents. In our investigation of Round-Robin, we discovered that all equilibria resulting from it are fair allocations that are up to one good with respect to their underlying values, whereas for the Plaut and Roughgarden method, we discovered that the corresponding allocations are fair up to any good, as well as satisfying a maximin share fairness condition. Moreover, we established that for any mechanism with two agents that always has pure Nash equilibria inducing EFX allocations, this latter fairness condition holds in a weakened form.

UGC 8839, an exceptionally faint spiral galaxy, is characterized by minimal star formation except in a substantial HII region located in the extreme outer rim of its disk. A comparative study with four similar spiral galaxies reveals that the unusual position of this star-forming region at such a great distance from the galaxy's center is likely unique to UGC 8839. Despite this distinct feature, the rest of UGC 8839 exhibits normal properties when analyzed with the other galaxies. The external dynamics of these galaxies were further investigated by calculating the mass-to-light ratios in different light intensity regions. The result shows a particularly low ratio of 0.06 ± 0.02 in a massive shell-like region, suggesting possible hyper-stability and requiring further investigation into possible explanations, including the potential for dark matter accumulation.

Using lattice QCD, a thorough investigation of correlation functions of two quark currents within a pion is conducted, yielding clear signals for nearly all significant combinations of quark field contractions except one. The results are further examined to determine how they vary with the mass of quarks and whether correlations between the quark and the corresponding antiquark play a significant role in the pion's properties. Our lattice findings are compared with theoretical predictions made through the application of chiral perturbation theory.

Evaluating protoplanetary disk evolution is closely tied to understanding how
mass accretion rates are influenced by a star and its disk properties.
However, accurately using observed relations in this context is hampered by
not properly accounting for variations in mass accretion rates, a problem
especially prevalent in earlier stages of star formation. Conversely, we found
extreme accretion variability in T Tauri system X Chameleone and observed it
over 11 days, with fluctuations reaching three orders of magnitude and showing
little long-term pattern. This behavior in X Chameleone is atypical compared
to other T T Tauri systems and may be related to the shape of its inner disk
or the nature of its surface layers. Given these findings and limited data
available, we chose not to include X Chameleone in our previous mass evolution
relation but instead presented it as a separate case study.

Offline learning for multiple interacting agents is crucial for developing
practical applications involving multiple interacting entities. Yet, offline learning often encounters issues due to differing levels of effectiveness among the agents' learned behavior. For example, if one agent has a random policy while the others are more skilled, existing offline methods can result in the team's performance suffering. To tackle this problem, we present a novel offline learning framework called Shared Individual Trajectories (SIT) that explicitly considers individual trajectories. The SIT framework leverages an attention-based mechanism to identify and share high-quality trajectories among the agents, thereby improving overall team performance when the input data comes from mixed distributions. Our approach has been shown to outperform the current state-of-the-art offline multi-agent learning models in simulated scenarios.

We developed a novel approach for registering MV images, utilizing a Convolutional Neural Network, to match the image content of kV images and assist radiation oncologists during stereotactic body radiotherapy. Since patient data for MV images is limited, making it difficult to achieve precise image registration, our approach leverages existing kV images for pre-training, under the assumption that the content of both images types is related. To incorporate the unique features of MV images, we fine-tuned the model with a modified loss function. Through comprehensive assessments involving data from multiple centers for prostate and lung cancer treatments, our fine-tuned approach outperformed various conventional registration techniques, achieving comparable results to state-of-the-art kV-kV image registration. Specifically, we observed lower normalized RMS errors for both synthetic and real 2D/3D MV image registrations, demonstrating that exploiting kV image content enhances the reliability of MV image-based registration. Moreover, our approach provided a consistent improvement of approximately 10% over automatic MV image methods for 3D/4D megavoltage images.

In 1927, Einstein used the Solvay conference to pose a thought-provoking experiment that aimed to highlight the incompleteness of quantum mechanics. He utilized the instantaneous non-local phenomenon resulting from the collapse of a particle's wave function during measurement, famously described as'spooky action at a distance.' Prior to the influential Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen critique of that era, he had taken an even more rigorous stance on this matter. This paper hails a significant advancement in understanding the non-local aspects of single-particle quantum mechanics, mirroring the groundbreaking contributions made by Einstein in the context of multiple particle systems at that time. We demonstrate that the inability of local realistic theories to fully explain the results of the EPS experiment for a single particle and the ensuing 'spooky' nature of the instantaneous non-local collapse was, in fact, originally pointed out by Einstein himself, back in 1927.

The integration of Artificial Intelligence techniques and improved information systems within Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) has yielded substantial benefits, albeit with heightened risks of security breaches and compromised privacy. As IoVs technology continues to evolve, there's growing interest in privacy preservation methodologies that adapt to these changes. Federated Learning has shown promise in safeguarding IoVs data and addressing concerns about security and privacy, whereas Blockchain technology presents possibilities for secure and verifiable data management. This paper conducts an in-depth review of Blockchain-Enabled Federated Learning frameworks for IoVs, exploring potential problems, viable solutions, and future directions. This comprehensive survey can serve as a blueprint for developing novel BC-Enabled FL solutions to address various IoVs data privacy challenges and scenarios.

V392 Persei, classified as a dwarf nova that underwent a classic nova explosion in 2018, is an extraordinary object of study. Spectroscopic analysis during the explosion's decline phase revealed anomalous abundances, notably underrepresented oxygen and lithium levels but also unexpected heavy elements like iodine and gold. Observational data from the Fermi and INTEGRAL \gamma-ray telescopes provided crucial insights, indicating V392 Persei as a high-energy source exceeding in brightness several other previously known nova explosions. Subsequent optical brightness surge in the visible light spectrum is suggestive of dense material around the binary system, potentially consisting of accretion disks on both sides. Following the explosion, the light curve exhibited a unique phase of rapid rem brightness recovery. Based on these observations, this research posits that V392 Persei could be a magnetar within a binary system, although an extremely massive white dwarf is also a plausible explanation.

A proposed precoder codebook and feedback encoding approach leverages Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) to construct codebooks and reduce information exchange between base station and mobile terminal. Initially, the base station trains a GMM using uplink signal samples, then creates a codebook based on GMM components, assigning one entry per component. Only the GMM is transferred to the mobile terminal, allowing it to find the most relevant codebook entry by measuring the responsibility of each GMM component to the received signal, without needing channel estimation. Feedback is transmitted as the index of the most responsible component and corresponding codebook entry, leading to enhanced performance over traditional approaches, notably in scenarios with limited pilot data transmission.

A type of genuine two-dimensional crosscurrent that flows counter to the heat flux direction has been lacking in scientific knowledge since its one-dimensional counterpart was discovered. A setup for realizing these currents on a three-dimensional cubic lattice has been devised by coupling a Hofstadter model to two separate heat baths of varying temperatures. Research demonstrates that the robustness of these currents can withstand various imperfections and tilting within certain nonequilibrium conditions, resulting in a pattern of current temperatures that exhibit robustness at a specific point of inflection. Additionally, the condition of being robust in the discrete quasicrystalline quenching model holds true for the robust currents in a three-dimensional space.

For asymptotically flat spacetimes, where light is emitted at a distance from the gravitational source, research indicates that the Bondi mass aspect must satisfy specific requirements to reach the point of infinity without obstruction. In general relativity, such constraints result in an upper limit on the mass change rate in relation to the speed of light and gravitational constant, leading to an interesting insight into Dyson's maximum luminosity theorem. In contrast, the conditions under which scalar gravitational waves in Brans-Dicke theory allow light to escape infinity without being overpowered by rapid mass loss.

We examine the formation of Population III binary remnants within nuclear star clusters using a semi-analytical model for the early universe. Our framework accounts for the movement of Population III binary remnants during the formation of the universe's structure and identifies which of these remnants fall into nuclear star clusters through gravitational interaction with field stars. Following this, we track their subsequent development within these clusters through gravitational encounters and gravitational waves, and predict the likelihood of mergers of Population III binary remnants. Our study shows that about 7.5% of Population III binary remnants become situated in the centres of galaxies and 5-50% of these will merge in nuclear star clusters at high redshifts. These events peak at z=5-7 with a merger rate of 0.4-10 years^-1 Gpc^-3. Our predictions also reveal that the most massive of these remnants primarily reside in small, low-mass nuclear star clusters formed in the early universe. These clusters host black holes of masses 40-85 M_\\odot that spin at rates of 0.3-0.6, which will be detected by LISA as they merge with companions of similar masses and spin rates.

In this study, we examine the security risks associated with wireless communication systems that use dual hop OFDM technology. To mitigate this issue, we analyze two main cases: one involving a single user with a single relay, and another with multiple users and relays. The primary goal of this investigation is to determine optimal power allocation methods across various frequencies in order to enhance end-to-end data transmission security while adhering to power consumption constraints at both the sender and relay nodes. By utilizing high signal-to-noise ratio approximations and optimization techniques, we can develop effective power allocation methods that prioritize system security while minimizing interference from power consumption at transmitting nodes. Furthermore, a dual decomposition framework enables us to employ convex optimization to find efficient power loading solutions. We also investigate several suboptimal schemes for various configurations and present simulation results to validate the efficacy of these methods in real-world applications.

Text-based games provide a rigorous platform to assess virtual agents in tasks like natural language understanding, solving complex problems, and applying real-world knowledge.
One significant limitation of existing text-based games lies in their slow speed, topping out at around 300 actions per second, largely because of outdated technology used to create them.
Our research presents TextWorldExpress, a highly optimized version of three widely used text-based game challenges, achieving a remarkable increase in simulation processing speed of roughly three orders of magnitude.
On ordinary computer hardware, it can process over one million actions per second, allowing for extensive tests lasting merely a day rather than weeks or even months.

Deep learning models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) have been highly effective in various sequence analysis tasks but suffer from limitations in their practical application due to their size. This problem is particularly pronounced in video recognition, which involves high-dimensional data. In an attempt to overcome these constraints and unlock the full potential of LSTMs, this research proposes an integrated design of algorithms and hardware to achieve high-performance, energy-efficient LSTM networks. At the algorithmic level, a new LSTM structure called FDHT-LSTM is developed, which significantly reduces model complexity without sacrificing accuracy. In addition to this optimized algorithm, a customized hardware platform is also designed to efficiently execute the FDHT-LSTM model by incorporating a sophisticated memory access scheme that minimizes data conflicts and allows for real-time matrix transformations. Experimental results indicate that this integrated design outperforms existing compressed models by achieving nearly identical accuracy to the original LSTMs, while also reducing inference times and increasing energy efficiency by a factor of 10 to 80 on the hardware platform.

The concept of the Weak Gravity Conjecture is often expressed through its effect on the mass-to-charge ratio of a particle. Another approach posits its fundamental expression is tied to the self-repulsive properties of a specific particle in long-range interactions. A new, closely related formulation suggests it could be formulated in terms of interaction energy. Specifically, a particle must interact with a point of like charge with an energy density that is always repulsive. This new interpretation of the WC helps clarify a puzzling aspect of the AdS/CFT correspondence, where the conservation of the stress tensor leads to a conservation of charge that appears to contradict a volume element with the same sign as the interaction energy. We demonstrate that for a wide range of theories in 4-dimensional spacetime, the relevant stress tensor conservation equation generally produces an indefinite result, thereby allowing states with a net non-zero charge to exist within a compact space, such as a sphere, and ultimately leading to an infinite self-energy in the sphere.

Given a Noetherian local ring with a specific prime characteristic and its primary ideal in terms of an $\mathfrak{m}$-primary parameter, we establish criteria for $F$-rationality based on the tight Hilbert function of that ideal. These criteria make use of a specific polynomial and its coefficient. Additionally, we provide a lower bound for the tight Hilbert function under the condition that the ring has a specific dimension.

The rapid transformation of the electricity sector necessitates innovative ancillary services that guarantee the stability and dependability of the electricity network. Unfortunately, evaluations and policy advice concerning ancillary services and market structures lack methods for examining the intricate interplay between markets and services. This paper presents an ancillary services acquisition model integrating both electricity and frequency services markets. The model facilitates the exploration of various market structures and policies by enabling the supply response to be modeled, thereby facilitating the assessment of supply interactions and offers advice on supply diversification. Additionally, the paper introduces a new type of supply competition spillover known as the negative inertia effect, which has not been previously identified. The proposed model and the new effect are applicable beyond the electricity sector and can be utilized to analyze other sectors with similar market dynamics.

R.W.K. Odoni initially established the connection between the Galois group of an iterated polynomial and the symmetric group in fields of characteristic zero. A generalization to fields of positive characteristic was achieved by Juul. Building on these findings, we explore a scenario involving an irreducible polynomial F over the algebraic closure of a finite field k(t) with algebraic and separable coefficients. When a generic monic polynomial Phi is composed with F, resulting in a new polynomial with coefficients (a0, a1,...), we identify the Galois group of the composite polynomial's mth iterate. The structure of this Galois group mirrors the (m-folded) iterated wreath product of the symmetric group S_(nd) for n > 0, where n represents the polynomial's degree. In the case of large finite fields, the application of this discovery aligns with analogous theories, including the polynomial equivalent of the Bateman-Horn conjecture, the Chowla's conjecture regarding autocorrelation, and the Chebotarev density theorem over function fields.

Saturn's polar atmosphere is characterized by seasonal variations of large warm whirlpools north of 75 degrees latitude. The strongest of these appear during Saturn's summer and disappear in the winter. The extensive exploration of the Saturn system enabled by the Cassini spacecraft has facilitated a comprehensive study of the formation of the North Polar Stratospheric Vortex through the application of infrared spectroscopy. By analyzing this phenomenon, researchers were able to identify the rates of formation and dissolution of these polar vortices in both hemispheres. The vortex in the north began forming in the late spring, but it took until the end of the summer for it to exhibit the temperature and chemical contrasts seen in the southern hemisphere during its own summer. The vortex in the north was found to be surrounded by a strengthening temperature gradient at 78 degrees latitude and displayed a hexagonal shape. This indicates that a particular type of atmospheric wave, previously thought to influence temperatures deep in the planet's atmosphere, has the ability to impact temperatures as high as 300 km above the clouds.

This paper investigates solutions to the Schrödinger equation under the influence of a focusing nonlinearity with mass-supercritical properties, in a domain exterior to a compact convex obstacle in a higher-dimensional space. We demonstrate that solutions with negative energy will inevitably collapse within a finite time period. Additionally, under the assumption that the nonlinearity is not too strongly energy-dependent and given specific symmetry conditions, we establish the same optimal blow-up criterion found by Holmer and Roudenko for solutions in an infinite domain. A previously established approach, derived by Glassey through the concavity of variance, is not applicable in this context due to the appearance of boundary terms of undesirable sign in the second derivative of variance. Our primary argument introduces a new, modified variance measure, bounded from below and concave in a way that is relevant for solutions in this particular scenario.

We provide a novel proof that local characteristic-zero, semi-parametric embeddings for a polynomial variety defined over the integers have an equivalent form to local positive-characteristic reductions of the variety for nearly all prime numbers.

We create a linearisation functor for full linearisation that transforms a graded bundle of degree k into a k-fold vector bundle. This function has an opposite, a process to make a k-fold vector bundle into a graded bundle, which provides its domain with a Poisson structure of degree |k|, effectively linking these structures.

This informal note begins by illustrating some technical concepts, including the re-normalization of measures on orbital integrals from the works of Langlands, Frenkel-Langlands-Ng\^o, and Altug's research on Beyond Endoscopy. We discuss specific measures related to algebraic tori and explain how they relate to Tamagawa numbers. We then examine the GL2 case in depth. Additionally, the appendix by Matthew Koster clarifies the connection between the geometric measure of orbits and Kirillov's measure of co-adjoint orbits within the dual space of certain Lie algebras, including sl2 and so3.

The interaction between light and matter is used in various spectroscopic techniques to extract details about a sample's molecular, atomic, or nuclear components. Although scattered light conveys both amplitude and phase information, this phase information is frequently lost during standard intensity measurements, yet it is crucial for reconstructing essential details of a target, as evident from applications like coherent x-ray imaging. A new algorithm is introduced that allows for retrieving phase information from one-dimensional time-resolved spectra, which significantly simplifies using spectral imaging tools in certain situations, as often encountered in x-ray absorption near edge structure measurements. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated with data from an x-ray beamline experiment, in which samples were generated as it moved from steel to an explosive yield state.

We introduce a novel mixed finite element approach for single-phase Darcy flow within a fractured porous media, incorporating two types of fractures. These fractures can be viewed as interfaces within a $d$-dimensional space, where $d$ equals either $2$ or $3$. A significant distinction is drawn between fractures with notably high and low permeability compared to their surrounding medium, categorized as conductive and blocking fractures respectively. Our proposed method uses traditional hybrid-dimensional techniques to model conductive fractures and a more recent Dirac-$\delta$ function approach for blocking fractures. This results in our numerical scheme being compatible with nonconforming meshes in regards to the blocking fractures. A major characteristic of our method's output is that the pressure and flux variables belong to continuous function spaces, thereby eliminating the need for post-processing to recover their continuity. This is particularly beneficial when considering applications where permeability fields are evolving and require a nonconforming discretization. Our method's efficiency and accuracy are demonstrated through comprehensive numerical experiments.

Hypothesis evaluation plays a significant role in cognitive science, where Bayes factors can compare and contrast competing theories by assessing their consistency with available data. However, implementing Bayes factor analysis is often complicated and heavily dependent on the accuracy of computational models' predictions. We aim to facilitate the creation of Bayes factor analysis for cognitive science projects that involve experimental data and computational modeling using Bayes factor extraction workflows in R with Graphite. These workflows enable non-trivial Bayes factor calculations to be automatically executed, leaving researchers free to concentrate on more critical aspects of their studies, including model selection and data collection. We will present various features of Graphite, demonstrate Bayes factor extraction from cognitive science-related computational models, provide essential Bayes factor analysis guidelines, and present case studies utilizing Bayes factor extraction workflows in cognitive science-related open-source packages.

Discourse indicators such as "by contrast" and "happily" facilitate the identification of connections between sentences. To improve the effectiveness of sentence representations in classification tasks, research has been done on predicting these indicators between sentences. This work diverges from this approach by using a trained model to forecast suitable indicators between sentences that have an established semantic connection, based on existing datasets used in research on discourse indicators. These predictions enable the exploration of the relationships between sentences, with existing indicators categorized into five groups: addition, subtraction, transformation, contrast, and continuation. When applied to a public dataset, the proposed method surpasses the effectiveness of random selection, with results indicating that approximately 27% of inter-sentence indicators correspond to contrastive relationships. Furthermore, discussion topics are proposed for each category of indicator that have been successfully predicted, with a focus on a new model for discussing a wide range of subjects derived from the statistics generated by the discourse indicators.

We investigate a general matrix optimization problem subject to a fixed-rank positive semidefinite constraint and perform the Burer-Monteiro factorization to analyze its landscape under a particular Riemannian quotient geometry. Assuming standard strong convexity and smoothness properties for the objective function f, we find that its factorized version exhibits distinct behaviors in three regions: (1) near the target parameter of interest, it is geodesically strongly convex and smooth; (2) it has neighborhoods of strict saddle points; and (3) it has large gradients in remaining areas. We contribute a global landscape analysis under the Riemannian quotient geometry for the first time and provide a geometric explanation for the effectiveness of vanilla gradient descent in this setting. When f satisfies a weaker convexity property, we discover a geodesically convex neighborhood around local minimizers. To achieve these results, we analyze a matrix factorization problem with a least squares objective, providing a critical connection, algorithmic application, and geometric insight.

A graph's edge coloring can be described as assigning different colors to edges based on a specific distance criterion, effectively mirroring the requirements of a certain vertex coloring in a transformed version of the graph. This notion was initially proposed as an open problem by Faudree, Schelp, Gyárfás, and Tuza in 1990, assuming a bipartite graph of high enough girth and a specific degree constraint could be colored using a certain number of colors, but in 2021 this was contested. Now, another example is given which also contests the conjecture originally presented by those authors.

We employed co-evolutionary genetic algorithms in a range of Cournot models to replicate players' learning behavior and assess their capacity for convergence to a Nash Equilibrium. Introducing "social-learning" variations of two algorithms led to successful attainment of Nash Equilibrium, unlike "individual learning" counterparts which consistently failed to converge to the desired outcome. Utilizing simulation outcomes with a specific approach as well as general statistical analysis, our results showed that "social" learning versions resulted in an ergodic Markov Chain, whereas "individual learning" did not. Our findings also highlighted that "social" learning versions are more efficient in reaching the desired state compared to "individual learning". Ultimately, our data indicates that "social" learning equivalents achieve the desired outcome within approximately 1/8th to 1/10th of the time required by "individual learning".

Consider a weighted directed graph, denoted as $\mathcal{D}$, and the edge ideal associated with it, labeled as $I(\mathcal{D})$. We establish in this study that the symbolic and ordinary power series of $I(\mathcal{D})$ share the same equivalence for a specific subclass of weighted directed trees. Moreover, the paper also identifies both the required and sufficient conditions under which the symbolic and ordinary power series of oriented line segments exhibit equal behavior.

Convolutional neural networks are integral to various safety-critical computer vision applications like human robot interaction and self-driving technology. Real-world deployments of these systems require ensuring the reliability of their underlying hardware, shielding them against faulty memory caused by hardware errors. Following the successful use of activation clipping, we have developed a prototype to automate this process by determining the optimal signal threshold beyond which error rates increase rapidly. Although this method involves several critical assumptions, we are seeking feedback on our approach to present a prototype and propose a path towards a formal safety case. We will demonstrate this by outlining required software-hardware testing, clarifying all critical assumptions, and presenting a functional case study where this method was applied to a classifier network.

Building upon the Jordanian twist concept, we have derived a generalized version. The generalized version, modified in the $r$-symmetrized format, meets the requirements for a 2-cocycle. Additionally, we have obtained specific formulae for its associated star product and twisted coproduct. Furthermore, we have established that our generalized version is equivalent to a 1-cochain-derived twist from the basic Jordanian twist.

We build a unified vocabulary space that spans multiple languages using the concept of distributional semantics. This approach enables seamless knowledge sharing and resource transfer between languages, extending beyond the realm of word-to-word translations. Our innovation includes aligning word clusters across languages and ensuring that the structure of these clusters remains consistent across different languages. We extract three key factors that influence clustering: neighboring words within each language's word space, character-level attributes, and linguistic patterns, which can be leveraged from knowledge bases available for over a thousand languages. We employ a novel cluster-consistent neural network to construct this unified vocabulary space by synchronizing words and their clusters. Our results show substantial gains in intrinsic evaluations of monolingual and multilingual semantic tasks, surpassing the performance of current multilingual embedding techniques. Moreover, an extrinsic evaluation using a case study on low-resource language name tagging demonstrates a 16.5% improvement in F-score compared to the existing multilingual methods.

The initial production measurement of various particles such as pions, kaons, 
protons and $\phi$ mesons in midrapidity for Xe-Xe collisions at 5.44 TeV is
reported. Extracted transverse momentum spectra and $p_{\rm T}$-integrated yields are
analyzed across several centrality intervals spanning from p-Pb to mid-central Pb-Pb
collisions based on final-state particle count. Investigating Xe-Xe and Pb-Pb collisions 
with similar charged-particle counts allows for comparison of initial geometric 
properties and flow behaviour. Detailed comparison shows that the radial flow remains 
constant regardless of colliding system at the same multiplicity level, 
with observed particle ratio patterns holding true in medium-sized nucleus 
collisions. Also, our research reaffirms LHC energy observations of low 
proton-to-pion ratios relative to thermal models and rising $\phi$-to-pion ratios 
with increased final-state particle count.

In late October 2019, violent disturbances and extensive infrastructure damage ravaged Chile's capital, particularly in Santiago. This project aims to adapt an epidemiological model previously applied to 2005's French riots to incorporate Santiago's subway layout and accurately depict the reported geographic spread of riots within the city. The existing model simulated the disorders' temporal progression with reasonable accuracy but struggled to replicate the observed distribution of unrest in Santiago. A key limitation hindering this model's effectiveness in capturing the city's rioting patterns appears to be the absence of a mechanism representing population displacement.

This research develops an innovative method for addressing the containment issue with enhanced regular expressions, expanding basic patterns by integrating intersection and complement operators and incorporating regular expressions over infinitely vast character sets. Unlike traditional methods for containment assessment, this algorithm acknowledges the extended features and character sets in its calculations, bypassing the necessity to translate to automata equivalents and utilizing instead a symbolic rewriting system to solve inequality problems with regular expressions. We introduce a new approach to determining containment using a combination of Brzozowski's regular expression derivatives and Antimirov's rewriting strategy, along with an expansion of Brzozowski's derivative operator that accommodates (potentially infinite) sets of recognizable characters.

Mobile agents require accurate and robust localization, and to meet this demand, Visual-inertial odometry (VIO) algorithms have been developed to estimate positions and movements using both camera and inertial sensors' data. These models, in particular the deep learning-based VIO ones, offer a high level of performance but with the significant drawback of requiring extensive training time and computational resources. To overcome this limitation, we propose an external memory visual-inertial odometry model that leverages deep learning, and we find that it ranks second to the top-tier end-to-end VIO approach on the TUM dataset.

Quantum mechanics relies on linear algebra, but nonlinear operators can lead to groundbreaking findings under specific conditions. In this study, we develop a new theoretical framework based on the parent Hamiltonians of the Weyl semimetal, which we call square-root higher-order Weyl semimetal, or SHOWS for short. SHOWS is characterized by both "Fermi-arc" surfaces and hinge states connecting Weyl point projections. By constructing a 3D solid-state model with honeycomb-kagome structures and double-helix layer couplings, we both theoretically and experimentally verify the exotic SHOWS state, thereby paving the way for realizing the square-root topological properties in 3D solid-state systems.

This study investigates the numerical solution to a problem of reconstructing incomplete boundary data for the time-varying Maxwell equations based on electric field measurements, where the goal is to recover missing information on the magnetic field. A quadratic cost function is used to measure the discrepancy between observed and reconstructed field data, subject to the Maxwell equations constraints. By replacing the original problem, which is highly complex, a sequence of simpler subproblems can be solved iteratively to obtain a sequence of approximate solutions. The validity of this approach is established through convergence analysis. Subsequent numerical experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness and stability.

This paper introduces the Federated Selective Aggregation (FedSA) challenge, a novel approach that allows the creation of a model equivalent to a target by combining parts of several data sets without sharing them. 
FedSA has significant potential for collaboration among organizations seeking to create a statistical model of a particular entity, such as a company, government, or institution, by combining their unique data sets. 
We propose solutions for FedSA that include a method to replicate the target's model when the number of participants is small and when they are numerous. 
To test our solutions, we develop a FedSA version of a popular image classification task and demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods in this setting. 
To facilitate further research, we make the code and results of our experiments available to the public.

We analyze the rank growth of elliptic curves from rational numbers to quartic extensions in the Galois groups $S_4$ and $A_4$, and investigate how rank varies in different quartic fields for a fixed elliptic curve. Notably, under specific conditions, we establish the existence of an infinite number of $S_4$ quartic extensions where the rank of an elliptic curve doesn't increase compared to its rank over the rational numbers. This achievement is made possible by our development of methods to manage the 2-Selmer rank of elliptic curves within certain quadratic fields, enabling control of the rank in families of $S_4$ and $A_4$ quartic extensions.

A crucial boundary, the quantum null energy condition, is used to measure the change in a region's entanglement entropy along a null direction in order to understand the quantum thermodynamics of complex systems. Investigating whether the quantum null energy condition limits irreversible entropy generation during quenching driven by an influx of energy and momentum from an infinite, memoryless bath, we find a condition that is equivalent to this quenching's isentropy. An investigation into an otherwise pure, two-dimensional conformal field theory reveals that this condition is met universally, providing a specific limit, particularly in scenarios where a spatial interval becomes entangled through a quench. This constraint also allows us to determine the minimum time it takes for quantum information to travel across a line in a holographic theory. Utilizing the dynamics of complex order parameters in a Ginzburg-Landau model with a negative mass term yields a concrete example where this constraint ensures the growth of entanglement.

We investigate the minimal time it takes for a qubit state to evolve from an initial state into a distinguishable state under both unitary and non-unitary dynamics. For unitary dynamics generated by a time-independent Hamiltonian, we develop a crucial criterion involving two asymmetry measures that ranks all possible Hamiltonians according to their ability to differentiate states. Notably, we identify three regions within the Bloch ball where the order of this distinguishability time varies based on the relationship between the Stefanescu-Serra and Mummey-Barrett asymmetry measures. For general time-dependent dynamics, we demonstrate that the minimal time for a state to become even marginally distinguishable can be effectively characterized using two average measures of operator asymmetry. For non-unitary dynamics caused by a trace-preserving completely positive map, we establish that the minimal time it takes for a state to become fully distinguished is directly related to the Barrett map asymmetry. For these dynamics, we also provide explicit examples and three-dimensional visual representations to better understand these concepts.

Consider a unit cube, $Q_n$, in $n$-dimensional space and a function space, $C(Q_n)$, consisting of continuous functions from $Q_n$ to $\mathbb{R}$. Define the norm of a function as its maximum absolute value over $Q_n$. Let $\Pi_1\left(\mathbb{R}^n\right)$ be the set of polynomials of degree at most one, i.e., linear functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$. An interpolation projector $P$ is introduced that maps functions from $C(Q_n)$ to linear functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$, using nodes within $Q_n$. When the number of nodes is an Hadamard number, a non-degenerate simplex can be formed with vertices at $Q_n$. Various methods will be discussed for establishing upper bounds for the norm of $P$ in the form $\|P\|_{Q_n} \leq c \sqrt{n}$ for the corresponding interpolation projector $P$.

Superconducting quantum circuits are emerging as prominent platforms for quantum computing. For practical applications, it is essential to address material flaws causing decoherence. This study employs terahertz Scanning Near-field Optical Microscopy to analyze the local dielectric characteristics and carrier concentrations in aluminum resonators on silicon substrates, critical components of superconducting quantum processors. Utilizing a vector calibration method, we determined the terahertz permittivity near the microwave feedline and found that etched silicon exhibits higher carrier concentrations than oxide etched silicon. We further investigate methods to reduce carrier concentrations, demonstrating the utility of near-field terahertz investigations in evaluating and identifying loss channels in quantum devices.

This work explores the long-term evolution of Venus's atmosphere, examining how its composition has been shaped by interior-exterior interactions over time. Despite significant ongoing research, key aspects of the atmosphere's formation and current state remain unclear and require interdisciplinary analysis. We examine various processes that have influenced the atmosphere's evolution, starting with volatile sources and examining interactions from the planet's core to its upper atmosphere, as well as atmospheric escape mechanisms. We also delve into the complex historical events that have contributed to the atmosphere's evolution, including the effects of impacts, magnetic field generation, and geochemical and geodynamic feedback cycles. We then outline plausible pathways for the planet's evolution, ranging from its accretion phase to its present state, using modeling and observations. These scenarios include atmospheric escape during the magma ocean phase, the effects of global melting due to runaway greenhouse effects, and the composition of comets and asteroids. We discuss the role of observations in testing our understanding of the planet's chemistry and geology, as well as the limitations of current data. Point processes that take into account multiple types of events, such as natural disasters, online messages, or neuronal activity, are used extensively in various fields. A key point process model that depends on the past occurrences is the nonlinear Hawkes process, which is used to model relationships, both excitatory and inhibitory, between events of different types. We have investigated a nonparametric Bayesian approach to estimating the nonlinear Hawkes process parameters, and have developed a variational approximation method for obtaining the process' posterior distribution. The proposed Bayesian method includes constructing Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and Generalized Likelihood Ratio tests to evaluate the proposed distribution and detect nonzero entries in the process' influence matrix. In a simulated event dataset, the Bayesian estimator showed high accuracy in reconstructing the true process and could effectively utilize the Generalized Likelihood Ratio test to identify non-zero entries in the influence matrix.

As high-power laser pulse capabilities increase, the limitations of traditional solid-state optics due to their restricted damage thresholds pose significant challenges, making the investigation of plasma-based components more compelling. We propose a novel type of plasma waveplate based on a specific magneto-optical property when subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field, allowing it to function under extremely high laser intensities. This component can modify the laser pulse polarization while simultaneously increasing the peak power, which has been demonstrated numerically with simulations. It shows that a high-intensity linearly polarized laser pulse can be converted to a higher-powered circularly polarized pulse. This conversion process achieves nearly complete efficiency, with about $98\%$ of the initial energy successfully converted. The required waveplate thickness was found to be inversely related to the electron density in the plasma and the strength of the magnetic field. This type of plasma waveplate may find a wide range of applications in a variety of laser-driven scenarios.

Re-examining the search for a nonzero electric dipole moment (EDM) form factor, $d_\tau(s)$, in $\tau^+\tau^-$ production via $e^+ e^-$ collisions between the $\tau$-pair threshold and $\sqrt{s} \approx 45$ GeV is made possible with the use of $\tau$-polarization. The expected sensitivity for JLAB-12 at CERN, JLAB-20 at JLAB, and Super $\tau$-Charm at JLab for $d_\tau$ is as follows: JLAB-12 can achieve down to $|d_\tau| \gtrsim 1.5 \times 10^{-19}$ cm, JLAB-20 can probe $|d_\tau| \gtrsim 4.5 \times 10^{-22}$ cm with polarizations of $\mathcal{P}_e \approx \mathcal{P}_\tau \approx 80\%$ and an integrated luminosity of $\mathcal{L}_{\rm int} \approx 50$ fb$^{-1}$, and for higher integrated luminosities of $\mathcal{L}_{\rm int} \approx 300$ fb$^{-1}$, it can reach $|d_\tau| \gtrsim 1 \times 10^{-22}$

We investigate decoding of rank metric codes under the assumption of a symmetric error matrix. Our analysis yields two main conclusions. Firstly, we show that for code rates less than half, there is a diverse class of rank metric codes capable of accurately decoding any symmetric error, even those of maximal rank. Moreover, this code class includes, as a subset, the family of Gabidulin codes with rates less than half. Secondly, we propose a method for correcting symmetric errors of up to n-k rank, which can be applied for code rates greater than half. Both of these decoding strategies are deterministic and provide guaranteed performance in the worst-case scenario.

Building upon previous work by \cite{Ferrara:1971vh}, \cite{Ferrara:1973vz}, we develop a comprehensive integral representation of conformal block operators in CFT$_2$, specifically tailored for spinning primary fields. Notably, this integral expression can be re-expressed as a product of two weighted AdS$_2$ field combinations when the primary fields in question are conserved, which results in the representation of conserved current conformal block operators in CFT$_2$ in terms of geodesic operators defined within the AdS$_2$ framework. Moreover, this new perspective enables a direct link between the AdS$_2$ geodesic operator representation of CFT$_2$ block operators \cite{Faulkner:2016u9i}, and the recently introduced lightcone AdS$_2$ block operator representation \cite{Guo:2020lxr}.

In 1992, Gelfand and MacPherson established a local and combinatorial approach to calculating Pontrjagin classes for differentiable manifolds. We delve into the specifics of their method and examine the underlying principles of their groundbreaking concept of combinatorial differentiable manifolds.

We obtained high-cadence photometric and spectroscopic data for SN~2020jfo in various wavelengths starting around day 3 up to day 434 after its explosion. SN~2020jfo, classified as a hydrogen-rich Type II supernova with a short plateau duration, had a notably faint absolute peak magnitude compared to other similar supernovae. Observations during the plateau phase revealed characteristic H-alpha absorption similar to other Type II supernovae. Furthermore, SN~2020jfo exhibited a complex spectrum during its declining phase that has also been observed in other supernovae, allowing us to estimate an electron scattering opacity close to its expected value. Additionally, we observed the interaction of stellar wind with the supernova shock around day 416, and estimated the mass of ejected material to be around $0.07$ solar masses based on the analysis of light curves and spectroscopy. SN~2020jfo's progenitor was determined to be a star with a mass ranging from 20 to 35 solar masses with an estimated absolute magnitude of $-1.56$.

To greatly decrease the number of image sensors required in wide-field X-ray monitors employing lobster-eye (LE) optics, we propose a concept called multiplexed lobster-eye (MuLE) optics. This configuration involves dividing an LE mirror into multiple sections and using each one to direct X-rays onto a single shared image sensor. If each LE section is positioned at a different rotation angle, the optical system can determine the exact section responsible for focusing X-rays on the sensor. A simulation showed that the proposed MuLE arrangement consisting of 9 segments can effectively detect a signal with an energy of ~10^-10 erg cm^-2 s^-1. Furthermore, this system is highly effective in determining the source direction of an X-ray transient, which is a critical requirement for the LE-based wide-field detectors. MuLE optics offers a simple design that is well-suited for implementing a next-generation wide-field X-ray monitor with a large field of view.

We establish a level set formulation for partial uniform ellipticity with symmetric concave functions, implying that key results in this area can be reinterpreted and proven with greater efficiency. This new framework allows us to recover and demonstrate in a more streamlined manner that solutions to certain non-linear second-order PDEs, specifically $F(D^{2}u) = f(u)$ in a domain $\Omega$, possess $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity properties, where $\alpha$ is a positive value.

To investigate the structure of dark matter, a deep learning framework was implemented and used to explore the impact of velocity and density information on the formation of halos through $N$-body cosmological simulations. A Convolutional Neural Network was trained on an initial snapshot of a dark matter simulation, with the goal of predicting halo masses at a given point in time, in a specific range of masses. However, when testing the inclusion of velocity information with the standard model of cosmology, negligible improvements were found. By increasing the amplitude of initial scalar perturbations in the simulation, a significant improvement was found in a higher primordially suppressed mass regime, with the combination of density and velocity fields offering a 4 orders of magnitude improvement in predicting halo masses at $z=0$ for halos with masses around $10^{10} M_{\sun} h^{-1}$. As such, this study implies that the combination of gravitational and velocity information from galaxy spectroscopic surveys can offer improved predictions of the distribution of dark matter halos in the universe on both large and small scales.

We have developed a novel numerical approach for achieving equilibrium configurations in rotating stars under the principles of general relativity. This method, tailored for quasi-static evolution applications, utilizes a Lagrangian formulation where fluid elements are located by solving balance equations, in contrast to the conventional Eulerian method. This innovative approach eschews the use of the Euler equation's first integral, often obtained analytically under simplifying conditions, in favor of assigning unique properties to each fluid element. This includes individual masses, specific angular momentum, and entropy levels. 

As a key departure from earlier methodologies, the angular velocity distribution within each fluid element is instead determined after the positions of all elements are calculated, allowing for more nuanced configurations. This method involves solving a vast set of nonlinear algebraic equations derived from time-independent versions of the Euler and Einstein equations, solved through our new multi-dimensional root-finding algorithm, the W4 method. 

We have successfully demonstrated our approach by generating equilibrium configurations in rotating stars under both barotropic and baroclinic conditions, and have also used this method to simulate evolutionary processes like stellar cooling, mass loss, and mass accretion, serving as basic models.

A major challenge in creating AI models that can automatically process and analyze visually complex documents such as invoices is acquiring a large, high-quality dataset to train these models. Our proposed approach, known as Selective Labeling, streamlines the labeling process by limiting the labels to simple "accept/reject" confirmations for model predictions made on partially annotated documents. This is paired with a specialized strategy for active learning, designed to identify and target model predictions with the highest levels of uncertainty. Our experiments on multiple document types across three different fields have shown that selective labeling can cut labeling costs by tenfold, without a noticeable decline in accuracy.

The collaborations of the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory and Virgo have observed the full spectrum of merging compact binaries, which comprise binary black hole, binary neutron star, and neutron star-black hole events. Combining these detections with electromagnetic radiation holds significant potential to improve our comprehension of neutron star events, particularly their dense matter state. However, electromagnetic analysis of gravitational waves necessitates the rapid identification of signals from gravitational waves in real-time. Traditional approaches struggle to achieve this at the rate expected for future detectors. We introduce novel results based on a deep learning approach, which employs a convolutional neural network to classify signals from real LIGO data involving neutron star and black hole mergers. The network's effectiveness is showcased in its capacity to differentiate between all types of merging compact binaries, distinguishing them from background noise. With approximately 500,000 training samples, we successfully trained a network that can recover 99.33% of neutron star and 99.44% of black hole signals, while sensitively detecting actual events in LIGO data. This discovery strategy is anticipated to achieve a lower detection latency than existing methods, which is expected to be crucial for the future of multi-messenger astronomy.

Urban settings are known to benefit economically and socially due to their diverse face-to-face interactions, which require close contact and spread easily within city populations. The COVID-19 pandemic, however, limited urban opportunities due to social distancing measures. Researchers analyzed mobile device data from 150,000 users in New York City to study how the city's daily encounters changed over the course of the pandemic. They discovered that while the pandemic initially caused a significant decrease in the city's physical presence and urban activity, these effects diminished over time as the population became accustomed to living in the city again. Surprisingly, although the pandemic did not affect the average size of the city's encounters, it led to a considerable deterioration in their diversity for a six-month period. This period was further found to be associated with an increase in COVID-19 cases in the following month.

Three-dimensional simulations of high-mass young stellar objects reveal that their surrounding gas shells, which are turbulent and contain large-density clumps, significantly impact their development. By analyzing the merger of two major gravitationally bound objects in a simulation of a stellar mass of 55 solar masses, the process of star formation in an episodic manner is examined. This in-depth examination of a merger event reveals that it results in a more intense outflow, which in turn produces broader emission from line spectra and affects the development of the protostar and its immediate environment. In addition, any detection of these spectral lines using future telescopes, such as ALMA, would most likely be possible for a brief window of time. It is hypothesized that the discovery of these features in the spectrum of a YSO could indicate the need to reconsider single-component models (gas or dust) in favor of more complex models that include bulk solid material, such as planetesimals. Moreover, it is suggested that the episodic accretion theory could offer an explanation for the ongoing development of massive young stellar objects.

This research investigates how a uniform shear flow influences the behavior of water waves in an infinite, two-dimensional domain, specifically those with nonzero constant vorticity. We sought to analyze how a uniform shear flow affects weakly nonlinear, surface gravity waves through the use of Hamiltonian formulation and Hamiltonian transformation techniques. By applying these methods to the water wave problem, we utilized a Birkhoff normal form transformation to determine whether the cubic-order interaction coefficient for the water wave equation's Hamiltonian form is non-zero. Our approach led to an explicit calculation of the cubic-order interaction coefficient, which we found is non-zero for all cases. As a result, the Dysthe equation in its Dansereau form applies to describe the slowly varying envelope of one-dimensional, deep-water gravity waves under a uniform shear flow, even in the presence of nonzero constant vorticity. Moreover, our finding indicates that solitons of the Dysthe equation experience the same frequency shift due to vorticity that was previously found to be true only for exact water wave solutions with nonzero constant vorticity, which we hypothesize is universally applicable.

In this proof, a modified Stokes formula for differential forms on locally convex spaces is presented, with the technique for establishing this result drawn from geometric variation theory. Additionally, a relevant expression from geometric quantum field theory is demonstrated to be equivalent to the integrand of the Stokes formula, presenting it for differentiation via tools from geometric variation theory.

Autonomous navigation in diverse and ever-changing indoor spaces poses a significant challenge for mobile robots. In poor weather conditions or when surfaces are obstructed, conventional sensing technologies may struggle to operate effectively and provide reliable data for secure route planning. A novel method has been developed to enable the navigation of indoor environments using a mobile robot with a sonar sensor, either singly or in combination, within a layered control framework. Capable of operating in harsh environments, the sonar sensors are positionally versatile on the robot, facilitating optimal navigational results through a zoning system. A key feature of this research involves presenting an acoustic flow model, along with a designed controller structure. Both theoretical simulation and practical testing on a mobile robot in an office environment, with real-time 2D navigation using one to three sonar sensors, are presented. Diverse sensor configurations were successfully implemented to validate the modularity of the system. Experimental results show that this method yields optimal navigational performance, with a modular design that enables the system to adapt to various indoor configurations based on the robot's external equipment.

The prevalence of false news is not a new issue but one that is expanding at a rapid pace. Social media has fueled the spread of misinformation by offering convenient access, coupled with limited fact-checking mechanisms. Given the negative consequences of this type of information on society, pinpointing false news has become increasingly vital. We propose an innovative method that leverages transformer-based language models to counter one of their inherent drawbacks, allowing our CMTR-BERT framework to combine diverse text representations, mitigate the sequential constraints inherent to the underlying architecture, and integrate contextual information effectively. Experimental evaluations using two disparate, publicly available datasets showcase our method's capability to achieve superior performance benchmarks, highlighting the benefits of leveraging automatic text summarization to integrate features for enhanced performance.

This research investigates complex systems that follow stochastic patterns by using mathematical structures known as random field models. The study focuses on analyzing a specific aspect of these systems – the geometry of their parametric space – using statistical tools to simulate and model the systems' dynamics. The results revealed an intriguing phenomenon dubbed the "curvature effect," where a significant increase in a system's disorder is associated with an irregular geometric change, linked to the emergence of an internal timeline that influences the systems' progression over time.

When applying dimensionality reduction techniques to datasets with anomalies, L1-PCA has been a well-liked alternative to conventional PCA due to its robustness in recent years. This study focuses on an under-explored version of rotationally invariant L1-PCA and develops an iterative optimization approach using proximal alternating linearized minimization and a form of extrapolation tailored to its two-block representation. Moreover, the algorithm is theoretically proven to converge linearly to a stable point, and this result is guaranteed to correspond to a minimum of the original problem when the algorithm's step size meets certain criteria. To support and validate the methodology, both artificial and real-world data were used in numerical experiments to illustrate the algorithm's performance.

Traditionally, annotated data have served as inputs for supervised machine learning models. Yet, contemporary pre-trained natural language processing models possess linguistic knowledge that can, in turn, be leveraged to guide the annotation process. In this work, we employ BERT, a neural language model, to facilitate the semantic labeling of a game-based interaction dataset called EMO20Q. Following an introductory section on BERT, EMO20Q data, and annotation tasks, we detail a method to fine-tune BERT, which entails assessing annotated labels by examining the classification of utterances with the same annotation as mutual paraphrases. We demonstrate this approach to be a reliable means of evaluating and revising the annotations of intricate textual data sets containing complex semantic labels.

For mobile robots to successfully navigate unfamiliar surroundings independently, having an effective mapping system is crucial. Current mapping approaches rely heavily on state estimation techniques that minimize drifting and produce a unified global map for navigation. Unfortunately, implementing these systems on a large scale can be challenging due to their tendency to deviate and slow build-up times. In response to these limitations, a novel map representation called HiTMap is presented, featuring a unique hierarchical structure that focuses solely on a local metric map for obstacle avoidance while keeping a graph-based representation of the environment to identify and traverse corridors. While this may seem like it produces a limited graph for navigation, its potential is amplified when a mobile robot moves through complex environments with multiple corridors. In comparison to alternative systems that learn and reproduce environment layouts, HiTMap offers a distinct advantage by retaining all environment information, thus providing a significant benefit for scale navigation. To demonstrate the effectiveness of HiTMap, a system that integrates this map representation for navigation is developed and tested on simulated and real-world environments, focusing on three distinct scenarios.

One of the key challenges in metrology lies in accurately measuring weak local magnetic fields expelled from superconductors through the Meissner effect. A Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometry system can be employed to sensitively detect these minuscule magnetic fields. As a superconductor's expelled field generates a gradient near its surface, it induces a centripetal force that affects atomic motion within the interferometer, making it possible to measure this effect through atomic interference patterns. Based on the $10^{-12}$ g accuracy achieved in atomic gravity measurements, it's theoretically possible to measure expelled local magnetic field strengths at levels as precise as $10^{-14}$ Tesla.

In the case of a finite admixture model whose components and weights are unknown, techniques from stochastic convex geometry help us determine how the number of identifiable components changes in response to an increase in the amount of collected data. Additionally, placing a Dirichlet process prior on densities within a defined range enables us to recover a measure that narrows to the specific identifiable components, thereby yielding the corresponding admixture weights. A new algorithm is then proposed to accurately capture the complexity of data by utilizing only the minimum number of components necessary.

High-performance computing on SIMD devices, including GPUs, has historically been challenging for object-oriented programming due to inefficiencies in memory allocation and access.  Despite this limitation, a range of applications, including real-world programs with inherent object structures, have been overlooked for parallelization opportunities.  Our research identified a particular subset of object-oriented programming called Single-Method Multiple-Objects (SMMO), which can be efficiently parallelized on SIMD devices by executing the same method across multiple objects of a given type.  To facilitate easy adoption of high-speed GPU programming for average developers, we created the DynaSOAr CUDA framework specifically tailored for SMMO applications.  This framework includes a dynamic memory allocator that is both lock-free and parallel, a data layout domain-specific language (DSL), and a do-all operation that is both parallel and efficient.  As a result, DynaSOAr offers improved memory usage, reduced fragmentation, and superior performance to leading state-of-the-art GPU memory allocators by concurrently managing both memory allocation and memory access through atomic operations.  Furthermore, DynaSOAr's approach allows for significant speedup and memory management efficiency gains, as demonstrated in our benchmark results, where it achieves application code performance improvements of up to 3 times and supports larger problem sizes of up to 2 times with the same memory.

A comprehensive theoretical framework has been developed to predict the spectral characteristics of magnetic impurities located on the surface of a superconducting material. This material-specific model focuses on the Yu--Shiba--Rusinov (YSR) states and incorporates an orbital decomposition of the surface states to provide insights into the local spin structure. Our approach is rooted in first principles and accounts for all relevant electron-electron interactions. We applied this model to determine the electron-electron interaction parameters for Niobium and a Mn adatom on its surface, as well as for a Mn dimer on the Niobium surface. Notably, our model predictions for Mn and Mn dimer YSR state positions and spin configurations match the electron spectroscopy experimental data presented by Liu et al. (Phys. Rev. B 100, 115416) without necessitating any adjustments. Importantly, the YSR state spacing between the $\pm$ spin projections of a Mn adatom or Mn dimer is found to be $0.15$ meV in all configurations.

The NASA $TESS$ mission's comprehensive sky survey allows the detection of rarest transiting planetary systems. In a new discovery, we found a young star named TOI-712, hosting a system of four planets orbiting it. By analyzing $TESS$ data, the team established that the star rotates in about 12.48 days and has an age ranging from approximately $500$ million to 1.1 billion years. Observations from $TESS$ revealed three mini-Neptune-sized planets with distinct periods of $9.531$ days, $51.699$ days, and $84.839$ days. In addition, the team detected a fourth planet named TOI-712 d, which has a semi-major axis similar to Mars and an equilibrium temperature between $0 K$ and $40 K`. Given TOI-712's luminosity of approximately $0.024$ times the sun, there is a possibility that TOI-712 d could be a candidate for direct transmission discovery. The system also has an interesting configuration, with TOI-712 c orbiting the star more quickly than TOI-712 b, which is contrary to typical arrangements.
